tool_name: Linear — issue tracking and project management for product/engineering teams. Vendor: Linear Orbit, Inc. (linear.app).
target_user: Individual contributors and team leads — fully self-service. A developer or PM can sign up, create a workspace, invite teammates, and stand up a cycle without any admin/IT involvement. Admin role exists only for higher-tier governance (SSO/SCIM, billing, import/export); it is not a prerequisite for team setup.
setup_time_estimate: Minutes to a productive first cycle. Linear's docs and third-party reviews consistently describe onboarding as 'near-instant,' with new users 'getting started in minutes' (G2/Product Hunt reviews). For a single team running 1–2 week cycles, sign-up → first issue → first cycle is achievable in a single sitting; productionizing GitHub + Slack integrations adds minutes, not hours. Linear's Startup Program offers up to 6 months free on Basic or Business, reinforcing the 'try it before you buy it' model.
onboarding_wizard: Yes — a guided first-run flow. On workspace creation, Linear auto-creates a default team with the same name as the workspace, then prompts for: team name/identifier, members to invite, optional GitHub install, optional Slack install, and cycle cadence. The Start Guide ('linear.app/docs/start-guide') branches by role (admin vs. member vs. lead). A demo workspace is available so users can explore issues/projects/workflows without committing data; demo changes are local to the browser and reset on refresh. There is no Scrum/Kanban/SAFe framework picker — Linear is opinionated about cycles + workflow states.
template_library: Linear ships issue templates and project templates. Issue templates can be set as default per-team, so every new issue in that team is created from the template unless changed. Project templates cover common patterns (launch, research, design review, etc.). Templates are workspace-scoped and can be shared across teams within a workspace; they are not a marketplace-style gallery. Third-party guides (IdeaPlan, Linear docs) describe the library as small but high-signal — quality over quantity, consistent with Linear's design philosophy.
ai_assisted_setup: Limited at the setup moment; richer at runtime. Linear's 'Product Intelligence' AI suggests assignees based on prior similar fixes, links duplicate issues, suggests labels and project assignment, and summarizes long issue threads into key decisions/blockers. The 2026 AI capabilities also support deeplinking issues to external coding agents (e.g. Claude Opus 4.5) and a 'Linear Agent' with controlled access to the codebase ('Code Intelligence'). None of these auto-generate a team structure, cycle cadence, or workflow at signup — Linear's stance is that the setup is already small enough not to need AI to scaffold it.
hierarchy_config: Intentionally shallow and fixed: Workspace → Team → Issue, with Projects and Initiatives layered on top as cross-cutting groupings. Cycles are team-scoped time-boxes (sprints by another name). Workflow states are per-team and follow a fixed taxonomy (Backlog, Triage, Todo, In Progress, Done, Canceled, Duplicate) — you can add custom states within these categories and rename, but cannot redefine the category model. Setup time for the hierarchy is effectively 'as long as it takes to name your team.' There is no Portfolio/Epic/Capability layer comparable to SAFe.
multi_team_setup: Designed to scale by adding teams, not by introducing program layers. Users can belong to one or many teams; teams have their own issues, cycles, labels, and workflow. Cycles can be configured to follow the same schedule across teams, but the UI cannot show two teams' cycles in a single view simultaneously. There is no native ART/Program Increment concept. Initiatives + Projects provide cross-team rollup. Self-service scales cleanly to dozens of teams; coordinating 50–100+ teams under a SAFe-style program is acknowledged as a gap relative to Jira/Jira Align in third-party reviews.
admin_dependency: Minimal. Any member with the appropriate role can create teams, cycles, labels, projects, and issue templates. Admin role is required only for: workspace-level import/export (Settings → Administration → Import/Export), SSO/SCIM configuration (Enterprise plan), billing, workspace-wide integration credentials, and member provisioning at scale. A team lead onboarding their squad does not need to wait on a central admin.
permissions_model: Deliberately simple. Roles are workspace-level (Admin, Member, Guest) plus team-level membership. Linear has historically offered limited fine-grained ACLs by design — reviewers note 'advanced permission models that are simpler than what large organizations sometimes require.' SCIM 2.0 user provisioning is Enterprise-tier and requires SAML SSO to be enabled first. The simplicity makes adoption fast but is repeatedly cited as the gap that blocks Linear from displacing Jira at the largest enterprise scale.
import_capabilities: Self-service and well-supported. Linear ships native in-product importers for Jira, Asana, GitHub Issues, Shortcut, and Trello, plus a CSV path. There is also a CLI tool (@linear/import on npm; source at github.com/linear/linear) for advanced cases. The in-product import assistants retain more data than the CLI, support bulk delete of an import if it goes wrong, and require Admin access (Settings → Administration → Import/Export). Field mapping is opinionated: Linear maps Jira issue types and statuses to its fixed workflow categories rather than recreating arbitrary Jira schemes.
migration_story: Migration is positioned as a first-class self-service action via the 'Switch to Linear' / Migration Guide flow (linear.app/switch/migration-guide). Most documented Jira→Linear migrations are run by the customer in a day or two for typical team-scale datasets; no professional services engagement is required. Reviewers describe migration friction more around Jira-specific concepts that intentionally don't map (sub-tasks beyond a certain depth, complex permission schemes, custom workflows with arbitrary states) than around technical import failures. For very large multi-project Jira instances, third-party migration partners exist but are not vendor-mandated.
vcs_integration_setup: First-class. GitHub: Settings → Integrations → GitHub, install the Linear GitHub app, authorize repos, enable auto-link/auto-close. Linear then auto-updates issue status on PR open/merge/close, supports magic words in PR titles/branches (LIN-123), and provides bi-directional links. GitLab and Sentry are also natively integrated. Time-to-first-linked-PR is on the order of minutes after install. Configuration is per-workspace and requires admin to install the app, but per-team behavior (which repos, auto-status rules) is configurable by team leads.
slack_notifications_setup: Self-service. Slack integration supports per-channel notifications on issue events (created, comment added, status changed, completed) and a 'More actions → Create Linear issue' shortcut from any Slack message. Any workspace member can wire their own channel notifications to teams/projects they belong to; admin involvement is required only to install the Slack app at the workspace level. Discord is supported on the same model.
first_impression_ux: On day 1 the user sees a clean, dense, keyboard-driven UI with a default team already created, a Triage inbox, a Backlog, an Active (current cycle) view, and empty-state prompts ('create your first issue' / 'set up your first cycle'). The interactive Start Guide and demo workspace let users explore without polluting their data. Reviewers consistently single out the first impression as 'fast, clean, and easy to adopt, especially compared with heavier tools like Jira, Asana, and ClickUp' (G2). The empty state is well-designed — it suggests the next action rather than just showing 'no items.'
time_to_value: Same session. The minimum viable setup is: create workspace → name the default team → create one issue → enable cycles → optionally connect GitHub. Value is felt within minutes. The free tier (unlimited members, up to 250 issues, basic kanban + roadmap + Slack/GitHub) lets a team prove value before any commitment. Standard at $10/user/month and Plus at $16/user/month gate advanced cycles, SLAs, and triage features, but the free experience is genuinely usable for a small team rather than a marketing-only stub.
setup_complaints: Most critical sentiment is not about setup itself but about Linear's opinionated model: (1) 'Fixed workflow states… you can customize labels but not workflow state categories' — felt as limiting once a team wants non-standard workflows. (2) 'Can feel too minimal… not many built-in customization or reporting options.' (3) Enterprise reviewers: 'advanced permission models that are simpler than what large organizations sometimes require,' 'less detailed audit logs,' compliance/reporting features 'still growing.' (4) Pricing complaint: 'Enterprise pricing is completely opaque… SCIM 2.0 only on Enterprise plan with custom pricing.' Notably absent: no recurring complaint about setup time, admin dependency, or learning curve.
setup_praise: Recurring praise on G2 / Product Hunt / Reddit: 'Onboarding with Linear is near-instant.' 'From the moment you log in, the clean, intuitive design shows that it's built to make work flow seamlessly.' 'Fast, clean, and easy to adopt, especially compared with heavier tools like Jira, Asana, and ClickUp.' 'Sub-100ms latency on virtually every interaction.' 'Every feature feels like it has a purpose, with no unnecessary extras bogging down the process.' Reviewers credit the local-first sync engine and the deliberate constraint-driven design for the day-1 feel.
standout_setup_feature: The combination of (a) zero-admin self-service team creation with an opinionated, fixed hierarchy, (b) sub-100ms UI responsiveness that makes the first 60 seconds feel different from every other tool, and (c) a usable free tier plus the Startup Program (up to 6 months free on Basic/Business) that lets a team prove value before procurement. The single differentiating moment is the speed: 'Linear delivers sub-100ms latency on virtually every interaction' because of the local-first sync engine — the setup doesn't feel like setup, it feels like already using the tool.
servicenow_comparison: Direct opposite of ServiceNow EAP on every setup axis: self-service vs. admin-gated, minutes vs. months, opinionated/fixed hierarchy vs. configurable SAFe topology, free tier with Startup Program vs. enterprise procurement, in-product Jira/Asana/CSV import vs. partner-led migration. Linear's gap relative to EAP is exactly EAP's strength: portfolio/ART/Solution Train governance for SAFe organizations and unified data with ITSM/HRSD/SecOps. [uncertain] No published case study found of an enterprise migrating ServiceNow EAP → Linear or vice versa; comparison is inferred from category-level Gartner Peer Insights and review aggregations rather than a head-to-head migration write-up.
